correctness.rationale: Exact rectangle+row-functional criterion derived both directions for arbitrary finite alphabets and overlapping lax splits. For each failure choose active row with two neighbors outside the active-row intersection, and active witness rows missing each; the three two-set lemma yields a disjoint-star or C6 false subteam. Direct calculation shows both shapes inclusion-minimal, and binomial counts label them without double counting. Standalone direct lax semantics compared on 848 teams; all minimal flags and coefficients tested on 74576 teams. Computation is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

evidence: Fröhlich–Kolaitis–Meier 2025/2026 examines two dependence atoms; its Theorem 25 concerns incoherence of different all-functional disjunctions.

Győrffy et al. 2024 define general edge partitions avoiding forbidden graphs, then analyze matchings, bicliques, and Ferrers classes, not the fixed mixed biclique/star-forest class or minimal-failure census.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General graph partitions or dependence-only coherence cannot be specialized mechanically to a mixed-atom formula: the first atom is not downward closed, and a one-sided star forest is neither a matching nor necessarily Ferrers. originality.rationale: Compared full relevant open primary literature and three highly similar published mathematical results by semantic implication. The published two-dependence-atom, inverse-dependence, and general partition results neither imply the mixed independence/dependence criterion nor its labelled 4/6 obstruction polynomial. Compared accessible prior mathematical statements for overlap, and searched exact and equivalent formulations. Remaining unknown equivalent older literature is disclosed.
residual_risks: Older graph-decomposition formulations under uncommon terminology may already imply the full formula; the accessible full texts and semantic searches did not reveal one.
Some older related texts could be inspected only in excerpts; structural separation and search coverage do not establish absolute historical priority.
